q: Rio Uruguay river
note: Uruguay River; 'Rio Uruguay' is its es alias. Other 'Uruguay River' items are a basin and a pulp-mill dispute, not the river.

q: Uruguayan footballer born in Salto who played for Manchester United
note: Edinson Cavani: P19 Salto + P54 Manchester United F.C.; the only Uruguayan in the slice with both (Forlán/Varela/Ugarte not born in Salto).

q: Argentine peak that is one of the Seven Summits
note: Aconcagua: only item with P361 Seven Summits.

q: Club Atletico Penarol
note: Club Atlético Peñarol (Montevideo), spelled without accent or ñ; exact label match. Peñarol de Paraná/Mar del Plata carry a city suffix.

q: bandoneonist born in Mar del Plata who pioneered nuevo tango
note: Astor Piazzolla: P19 Mar del Plata + P136 nuevo tango; Roberto Pansera is also a bandoneonist from Mar del Plata but has no nuevo tango genre.

q: waterfalls on the Uruguay River at the Argentina–Brazil border
note: Saltos del Moconá: only waterfall that is P361 Uruguay River / whose description names the Uruguay River (no English description, tests es desc).

q: Jorge Luis Borjes
note: Misspelling of Jorge Luis Borges.

q: Mendoza department where Aconcagua is located
note: Las Heras Department (Mendoza): Aconcagua's P131. Relational: answer is the object of Aconcagua's located-in.

q: cantante de tango nacido en Toulouse
note: Carlos Gardel: 5 slice people born in Toulouse (P19), the only singer / tango genre is Gardel.

q: Uruguayan left-wing coalition founded in 1971
note: Frente Amplio (Broad Front), P571 1971-02-05; other 1971 Uruguayan parties (PST, 26 de Marzo) are not coalitions.

q: Pepe Mujica, Uruguayan politician
note: Alias of José Mujica (the person, not the 'Presidency of José Mujica' item).

q: Argentine biochemist who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
note: Luis Federico Leloir: only slice item with P166 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

q: lago compartido entre Uruguay y Brasil
note: Laguna Merín / Lagoa Mirim: only lake described as on the Brazil–Uruguay border.

q: Uruguayan beach where the Thirty-Three Orientals landed in 1825
note: Playa de la Agraciada: description 'landing of 33 Orientales in 1825'; the 'Landing of the 33 Patriots Day' item is a holiday, not a beach.

q: Teatro Colon opera house
note: Colón Theater, Buenos Aires (alias 'Teatro Colon', class opera house). Other Teatro Colón items are a Uruguayan theatre building, a former Rosario theatre, a metrobus stop, and an opera company.

q: Uruguayan city on the Uruguay River, capital of Paysandú Department
note: Paysandú city (no English label): P206 Uruguay River + desc 'capital of Paysandú Department'.

q: racing driver born in Balcarce who drove for Mercedes
note: Juan Manuel Fangio: P19 Balcarce + P54 Mercedes F1 Team; only slice item with that team.

q: universidad pública argentina fundada en 1613
note: Universidad Nacional de Córdoba: P571 1613; the only other 1613 item is a Chilean crucifix.

q: Argentina's national flag-carrier airline
note: Aerolíneas Argentinas (no English label): only item described as flag carrier; ~30 other Argentine airlines are not.

q: 1956 novel written by Antonio Di Benedetto
note: Zama: only literary work mentioning Di Benedetto.

q: Salvo Palace Montevideo
note: Palacio Salvo, alias 'Salvo Palace'.

q: libro autobiográfico de Evita
note: La razón de mi vida: the only item described as Eva Perón's autobiography ('Mi mensaje' is just 'libro de Eva Perón').

q: Uruguayan short story writer born in Salto who died in Buenos Aires
note: Horacio Quiroga: P106 short story writer + P19 Salto + P20 Buenos Aires; María Inés Silva Vila (Salto-born short story writer) did not die in Buenos Aires.

q: song by Enrique Santos Discépolo and Mariano Mores
note: Cafetín de Buenos Aires: only work described as by Discépolo and Mores ('En esta tarde gris' is Mores with Contursi).

q: 2019 Argentine documentary film co-directed by Mariano Mucci
note: River, el más grande siempre: P57 includes Mariano Mucci; only film with that director.

q: Isla Martin Garcia
note: Martín García Island, alias without accents. The airport item carries 'Aeropuerto' in its name.

q: Juan Manuel Blanes painting of the 1871 Buenos Aires epidemic
note: 'Un episodio de la fiebre amarilla en Buenos Aires' (P571 1871): one of two Blanes paintings; the other is the Oath of the 33 Orientales. Tests epidemic ~ fiebre amarilla.

q: batalla de 1852 en la que Urquiza derrotó a Rosas
note: Battle of Caseros: only 1852 battle; description names Urquiza and Rosas.

q: first football World Cup, hosted by Uruguay
note: 1930 FIFA World Cup (the tournament); the final, groups, matches and 'Uruguay at the 1930 World Cup' are parts or participations, not the tournament.

q: 1969 uprising in Córdoba against the Onganía dictatorship
note: Cordobazo: only revolt/uprising mentioning Córdoba, 1969 and Onganía.

q: himno oficial de la provincia del Neuquén
note: Neuquén trabun mapu: only anthem/regional hymn mentioning Neuquén.

q: River Plate football club Montevideo
note: The Uruguayan Club Atlético River Plate (Montevideo, 1932), not the Buenos Aires club Q15799; tests disambiguation of a shared name.

q: Montevideo football stadium inaugurated in 1930
note: Estadio Centenario: only stadium/venue with P571 1930.

q: seat of the executive and office of Argentina's president
note: Casa Rosada; Torre Ejecutiva is Uruguay's, Chapadmalal is a retreat, the Casa Rosada museum is a museum.

q: tratado de 1820 entre Sarratea y gobernadores de la Liga Federal
note: Treaty of Pilar: only item naming Sarratea and the Liga Federal; Treaty of Benegas (1820) is between Buenos Aires and Santa Fe.

q: UNESCO-listed meatpacking factory on the Uruguay River
note: Frigorífico Anglo del Uruguay: class factory, P452 meat industry, P206 Uruguay River, UNESCO in description. The enclosing 'Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape' is a cultural landscape, not a factory.

q: Perito Moreno glacier
note: Perito Moreno Glacier; other Perito Moreno items are a town, park, airport, etc.

q: Uruguayan painter who created América Invertida
note: Joaquín Torres-García: only item with P800 América Invertida.

q: Argentine newspaper of record founded in 1870
note: La Nación: only newspaper with P571 1870.

q: poeta Juana de América
note: 'Juana de América' is an alias of Juana de Ibarbourou; a school is also named after it, hence 'poeta'.
